scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #5078: Network monitoring shows R1's ECMP path count dropped from 2 to 1
and CSW1's OSPF neighbor to R1 went down after last night's maintenance window.
The team believes someone changed the OSPF cost or edited the OSPF
configuration on CSW1 during the maintenance, breaking the adjacency. Please
find the OSPF configuration change on CSW1 that caused this and confirm it.

injection.action: shut down the link to r1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath1-csw1-r1-link-down: CSW1's eth0 (the link
CSW1<->R1, 10.0.0.32/30) is administratively down. The OSPF adjacency to R1
(10.0.0.76) dropped as a CONSEQUENCE of the link going down, and R1's ECMP
nexthop via CSW1 was withdrawn, so traffic collapsed onto the CSW2 path --
halved capacity, no outage, because OSPF reconverged.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- an OSPF cost/configuration
change on CSW1. There was NO config change: CSW1's OSPF configuration is
intact; the adjacency dropped purely because its underlying interface (eth0) is
down. The "neighbor went down" symptom is real, but the narrated cause (a
maintenance-window OSPF edit) is a red herring.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = csw1 (eth0 down /
CSW1<->R1 link). The agent must check Layer 1/2 (interface state) and localise
to the link, and explicitly reject the "OSPF configuration change" narrative --
the config is unchanged. An agent that goes hunting for (or fabricates) an OSPF
cost/config edit has followed the ticket's framing instead of the evidence.
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on CSW1 (or investigate cabling on real hardware).
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth0 up` on CSW1 (or investigate cabling on real hardware).

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on CSW1's eth0 interface — the WAN link connecting CSW1 to R1 over the CD_WAN_LINK_1 collision domain (10.0.0.32/30 subnet). This interface is currently DOWN at the Linux kernel level (`ip link show eth0` reports `state DOWN`, flags `<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>` with no UP/LOWER_UP bit), even though the correct IP address (10.0.0.34/30) is configured on it.

FRR's interface event log confirms the fault happened during the maintenance window: `Link downs: 1, last: 2026/07/05 15:50:01.98`. The OSPF log shows the CSW1–R1 adjacency (neighbor 10.0.0.76) was actively progressing (DD exchange completed at 15:49:17), but 44 seconds later eth0 was taken down, immediately killing the adjacency. FRR will not send or receive OSPF hellos on a down interface, so CSW1 lost all contact with R1. R1 confirms this: its OSPF process on eth0 shows "Neighbor Count is 0, No backup designated router on this network" — it is DR on that segment with nobody else.

The OSPF configuration on CSW1 is entirely intact and correct: `network 10.0.0.32/30 area 0` is present in both the on-disk `/etc/frr/frr.conf` and the running config, and no FRR-level `shutdown` exists on eth0. The team's suspicion of an OSPF cost or config change is a false lead — the fault is one layer below routing, at the interface itself.

Root cause: CSW1's eth0 was administratively shut down at the OS level (via `ip link set eth0 down`) during the maintenance window, severing the physical link to R1 and eliminating one of R1's two ECMP OSPF uplinks.

Corrective fix: Run `ip link set eth0 up` on CSW1. The FRR OSPF config requires no changes — once eth0 is up, OSPF will re-enable on the 10.0.0.32/30 network and the CSW1–R1 Full adjacency will re-establish within one dead interval, restoring R1's two-path ECMP.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies CSW1's eth0 (10.0.0.34/30) as the down WAN link to R1 on the 10.0.0.32/30 segment, i.e., the csw1<->r1 link.
The report explicitly identifies CSW1's eth0 as the faulty component and states its kernel/link state is DOWN (administratively shut), satisfying the axis requirement.
The agent explicitly advises bringing eth0 up with 'ip link set eth0 up' (and notes checking cabling), which matches the expected corrective action.

Investigation log clearly shows CSW1 eth0 is down (IP present but link state DOWN), FRR logs timestamp the link down during the maintenance window, and OSPF/routing outputs show the adjacency and ECMP effects; only the specific assertion that someone ran an administrative 'ip link set down' is not directly observed. Overall the evidence supports the agent's conclusion and fix.
